source: Written for english/y7 lesson 64 (Model paragraph and writing frame (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 64: Analytical writing: a PETZAAL paragraph on how Ali is presented. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

passage.title: Model PETZAAL paragraph
paras: The writer presents Ali as someone whose perseverance was tested by sacrifice. [Point] His title was 'stripped' [Evidence], a violent verb [Technique] that makes the loss feel sudden and forceful [Zoom]. The short sentence 'He did not give way.' [Technique] stands firm in the paragraph just as Ali did. [Analysis] An alternative reading is that the writer wants us to admire his faith as much as his boxing. [Alternative] This links to the article's idea that perseverance, not talent, finishes the job. [Link]

passage.title: Teacher-written biography extract for TGA
paras: In 1967, at the height of his fame, Ali refused to be drafted into the army, saying his religion forbade him to fight in the war. The cost was immediate: his title was stripped, his licence to box was taken, and for three and a half years he could not fight. He did not give way. When the Supreme Court cleared his name in 1971, he returned to the ring, older but unbroken.

model.title: How does the writer present Ali's conviction?

parts.text: Point and Evidence: The writer presents Ali as unshakeable: he 'did not give way'.
Technique: a short, plain sentence after a list of losses
Zoom in: 'unbroken' suggests something tested hard but not destroyed
Analyse: the losses pile up, yet his will holds
Alternative: some readers might see stubbornness, not conviction
Link: either way, his refusal defines his legacy

head: Not this
This
rows: Ali refused the draft and was banned. Then he came back in 1971.
The phrase 'older but unbroken' presents Ali's comeback as a victory of will over time: the ban aged him but did not defeat him.

keywords.def: the school's analytical paragraph frame: Point, Evidence, Technique, Zoom in, Analyse, Alternative, Link
build a quotation smoothly into your own sentence
a reading of what something means

questions.q: Embed this quotation: 'did not give way'
questions.a: For example: Despite losing his title, Ali 'did not give way'.
his title was taken forcefully, leaving him exposed

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write one PETZAAL paragraph: How does the writer present Ali's perseverance? Starter: 'The writer presents Ali as...'
Extend: add a second Zoom in on a different word
Stretch: write an Alternative that genuinely challenges your Point
questions.a: For example: a reader in 1967 might have called his refusal unpatriotic
A) his spirit survived great pressure. Unbroken implies something that faced force but did not break: his will, not his body.
